stemMd: Why does increasing temperature often speed up a chemical reaction?

options.label: B
options.textMd: Atoms change into different elements at ordinary reaction temperatures.

options.label: C
options.textMd: A larger fraction of collisions can overcome the activation-energy barrier.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The activation energy must become exactly zero.

explanationMd: Higher temperature changes the distribution of molecular energies, increasing the fraction able to cross the reaction barrier. This typically raises the reaction rate. It does not require the activation energy to disappear or the reactants to become catalysts.

distractorRationale.a: Heating does not turn every reactant into a catalyst.
distractorRationale.b: Ordinary heating does not cause the nuclear changes implied.
distractorRationale.e: A reaction can speed up while retaining a positive barrier.
distractorRationale.d: Collision frequency and effective collision energy generally do not vanish.
